title: What If Fewer Than 50 People on Earth Shared Your Blood Type?

scenes.text: What if fewer than 50 people on Earth shared your blood type? Doctors call it golden.
Rh-null blood has none of the Rh antigens the rest of us carry. It was first found in 1961, in an Aboriginal Australian woman.
By 2010, only about 43 people had ever been recorded with it. Roughly one in six million is born this way.
It's golden because it can be given to anyone with a rare Rh type. The catch: you yourself can only receive Rh-null blood.
Only about nine people in the world actively donate. A single bag may be flown across borders to reach one patient.
Your blood could save almost anyone. Almost no one could save you.

description:
What if your blood type were shared by fewer than 50 people on Earth? Rh-null blood, first described in 1961 in an Aboriginal Australian woman, lacks every Rh antigen; by 2010 about 43 people had ever been recorded with it, and only around nine actively donate.
It is called golden blood because it is a universal donor for rare Rh types, yet people who have it can only receive Rh-null blood themselves.

first_comment: There are dozens of blood group systems beyond A, B and O; Rh is just one of them. Do you know your full blood type?
